_meta.notes: FOUR nodes rather than one, and that is the point of the scene: the block used to draw a critical badge PER id, so this picture was four red alarms whose redness said nothing the first one said. Severity is a reading about the vehicle and the vehicle has one state here, so one badge carries it and the nodes are content beside it. One node could not show the defect and so could not show the fix. The four nodes also carry the three answers the wire distinguishes, deliberately, because each renders differently: a titled node with the parts waiting on it, which is the ordinary case and the operator's actual question answered; a titled node with an EMPTY parts list, which says so out loud because a node can be required by something other than a part; and an UNTITLED node, which falls back to its id because the wire leaves a missing title absent rather than substituting the id. The fourth node's parts list is absent, which draws nothing at all: that is the editor ship being unreadable, and no claim is available to make.

_scene.caption: A fully tooled spaceplane: no rollout because it does not roll out, no surcharge row because there is no surcharge, and four blocking tech nodes under ONE severity badge, each named and each showing what on the vehicle is waiting for it
